open_points.subject: refusal reasons
open_points.text: "a bounded reason naming the first failing check" and "the closed set of reason codes a refusal ... detail names"
open_points.question: What exact machine-readable reason values may accompany `refused` for each public operation?
options: Define one closed enumeration shared by all operations
Define a closed reason enumeration per operation
Treat the bounded reason as unrestricted diagnostic text
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed per-operation reason enumeration plus bounded diagnostic text.

open_points.subject: actor attribution on records
open_points.text: "Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27" and "The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record", while records such as NodeExecution, EffectAttempt and TrialExecution have no actor field
open_points.question: Where is the acting actor persisted for records whose State 1 model has no actor field?
options: Add actor metadata to every stored record
Add actor fields to the affected models
Infer the actor from related run, approval or recovery records
open_points.default_guess: Store actor metadata with every record rather than infer it.

open_points.subject: flow constants
open_points.text: Inputs say "constants with declared classes", but enforcement says "A constant's StoredValue takes the `value_schema` and class the composing agent declared with it"
open_points.question: Does `compose_flow_version` require each constant to declare its own `value_schema`, or is the schema taken from its target port?
options: Require a schema and class on every constant
Take the schema from the target port and require only a class
Infer both schema and class from the target port
open_points.default_guess: Require the constant to declare its schema and class, then prove that its value fits the target.

open_points.subject: canonical JSON parsing
open_points.text: `canonical_bytes` takes "One JSON value" but must refuse "a duplicate key"
open_points.question: What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` so it can detect duplicate object member names before an ordinary JSON parser has discarded them?
options: Accept raw JSON text or bytes
Accept a duplicate-preserving parsed representation
Require the surface parser to detect duplicates and remove that error from `canonical_bytes`
open_points.default_guess: Have the surface parser reject duplicates and pass an already parsed JSON value to `canonical_bytes`.

open_points.subject: pagination over mutable fields
open_points.text: "the continuation token is the store position of the last item returned" and filters include mutable fields such as `status`
open_points.question: What happens when records enter or leave a status-filtered list between pages, including when the record at the token's position no longer matches the filter?
options: Use live filtering below the stored position
Bind the token to a snapshot of matching records
Reject the token if its anchor no longer matches
open_points.default_guess: Use live filtering below the immutable store position and keep the token valid even if the anchor's status changed.

open_points.subject: trial file fixture inspection
open_points.text: "The owner receives every value" but "a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — [is returned] as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`", which "takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue"
open_points.question: Can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
options: Allow `read_spooled_file` to accept file-carriage StoredValues
Add a separate fixture-byte read operation
Fixtures are never readable as bytes after authoring or capture
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only operation for reading a file-carriage StoredValue fixture.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances scope
open_points.text: State 4 says "A selected service whose manifest record cannot be read stops the start", while State 5 says "The services checked are those the installation holds a credential for"
open_points.question: At startup, are manifest records checked for every selected service, every credentialed service, or only their intersection?
options: Every selected service, plus credential-name checks for every credentialed service
Every credentialed service only
Only services that are both selected and credentialed
open_points.default_guess: Check every selected service's manifest and perform credential-header checks for every credentialed service.

open_points.subject: prepare_request pre-send order
open_points.text: State 3 orders "a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed", while State 5 orders "a plain `http` target not allowed, a repeated required header"
open_points.question: Which failure wins when both the plain-HTTP policy and repeated-required-header check fail?
options: `plain_http_not_allowed` first, following A09 and State 5
`required_header_repeated` first, following the State 3 module text

open_points.subject: spool removal result
open_points.text: `release_run` says "The run's spooled files are gone", but also says "A spool that cannot be removed does not fail the request" and removal occurs at a later start
open_points.question: Does successful release or cancellation guarantee physical deletion before returning, or only make the spool logically inaccessible and schedule best-effort deletion?
options: Guarantee physical deletion and return `internal_error` if it fails
Return success after logical invalidation even if bytes remain until startup cleanup
Retry deletion within the request before returning
open_points.default_guess: Return success after logical invalidation and retry physical deletion at startup.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity
open_points.text: M22 says equal values require equal facts including digest, size and media type, while State 5 says "A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)"
open_points.question: Is SpooledFile identity the producing position alone, or the complete M22 fact set including content facts?
options: Producing position alone is the lookup identity
All M22 facts form its identity
Producing position is a key while the complete fact set defines value equality
open_points.default_guess: Use producing position as the record key and treat digest, size and media type as immutable attributes.

open_points.subject: direct `not_applied` attempts
open_points.text: M26 says "Sending again after `not_applied` is a new attempt under a fresh approval", but A13 makes a direct 4xx `operation_refused` a failed element and State 5 only selects fresh approvals after an attempt "resolved `not_applied`"
open_points.question: Can a direct 4xx attempt recorded `not_applied` ever be resent, or does the run fail permanently without a resend operation?
options: Only owner-resolved unknown attempts may be resent
Any `not_applied` attempt may be resent through a defined action
Direct 4xx failures may be resumed using `resume_run`
open_points.default_guess: Only an unknown attempt explicitly resolved `not_applied` may be resent; a direct 4xx fails the run.

open_points.subject: standing grant effect
open_points.text: `grant_standing_approval` says "Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval", while grants for `read` or `draft-write` are never used and every resend after `not_applied` requires fresh approval
open_points.question: What exact future sends does a newly granted approval authorize?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect sends that are not resends after `not_applied`
Every non-destructive send except a resend after `not_applied`
All sends of the node
open_points.default_guess: Authorize only state-transition and external-effect sends that are not resends after `not_applied`.

open_points.subject: orphaned content-addressed bytes
open_points.text: "When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay" while `put_value_bytes` publishes bytes before the later record change, and K-10 says the only files kept beyond a run are trial-case fixtures
open_points.question: If publishing value or fixture bytes succeeds but the record change fails, must the unreferenced bytes be removed, retained as inert orphans, or committed atomically with the record?
options: Remove unreferenced bytes before returning the internal error
Allow inert unreferenced bytes to remain permanently
Combine byte publication and record creation into one recoverable store operation
Remove unreferenced bytes during startup cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Allow inert unreferenced bytes temporarily and remove them during startup cleanup.
